435:
We checked the Docent's accomplices' addresses.
The helmet wasn't at any of them.
436:
That leaves our last lead:
Prokhorov, the cloakroom attendant.
437:
But we couldn't follow it up.
Prokhorov failed to appear at the meeting.
438:
He may have suspected something.
He quit his job and hasn't been home.
440:
We owe you a thousand apologies
and our deepest thanks. Take off the wig,
441:
wash off the tattoos, go home and celebrate
New Year. Thank you so much.
- And my men?
442: We'll take your charges back today.
443:
If you find the cloakroom attendant,
might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you, but Bely,
the real Docent, escaped from prison today.
445:
Unbelievable, but true.
It's dangerous for you to stay in disguise.
446:
Could it wait until tomorrow? It's New Year,
and they've tried, in their own way.
447:
We're out in the country.
It's unlikely the Docent will find us.
448:
All right, but don't leave the dacha!
Oh, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife. Here's her reply,
addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on the first, promise?
- We promise!
451:
Such a nice woman.
Shame her father's a fence and a profiteer.
452:
What's all the shouting? Who said you could go out?
- There he is... The bad man.
454:
The New Year is here. My wish for you
is that everything will be new this year.
455:
Anything can happen, but remember:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... One moment.
- Where's he going?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of him anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of? He's saying
he'll find us anywhere and slit our throats.
461:
They say he took a razor to Speckle's throat.
Slice, and goodbye!
- He's turned savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to visit you?
Father Frost, bringing presents for you!
463:
- Fedya, come here.
- What did I do?
- Come on. Wear these at home. Keep warm.
464:
- What do I need them for? I haven't got a home.
- You will. There's still time.
465:
- They'll come in handy in prison for now. Wear them.
- Always predicting the worst.
466:
This is for you, Vasya.
Gavrila Petrovich, this one's yours.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- And this is for you too.
469: Sour stuff. It's boring without vodka.
470:
- Must you get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit and talk
from the heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I'm not having
a heart-to-heart with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Get a load of him! You think I'm some sucker
who'll play cards with you? You've got nine aces.
474: It doesn't have to be cards.
475:
There's a good game called Cities.
I say "Moscow."
476:
It ends in W, so you say "Warsaw."
Then you say a city beginning with W. Got it?
477: Now your turn, Fedya. A city beginning with W.
478:
Vorkuta.
- Why? - I did time there.
479:
- All right. Now you: a city beginning with A.
- Dzhambul. - Why Dzhambul?
480:
Because it's warm there.
My home is there. My mother is there.
481:
Let's try this, then. I'll go out, you hide something,
and when I come back, I'll find it.
482:
- You'd do better to find our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it, and he'll peek through a hole.
- All right, you go out and hide something.
484:
And you make sure I don't peek.
- Why me? Everything's always Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your mouth off, you little rascal!
- Always my mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- You came on your own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I tried coming to see you,
but I sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Just keep walking.
495:
- Sorry we disturbed you for nothing, doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him valerian, warm tea,
and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, hello! We found out
you're in prison,
500:
and we were very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
What swine told the little one
that Khmyr was in prison?
502:
"Mom was happy too. When your letter came,
she cried all day.
503:
Before that, she told us
you were a test pilot."
505:
"But I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506:
you're a good man,
but you're weak-willed."
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed enough to steal
our money and blame the taxi driver.
508:
Scram! I'll knock your horns off,
you rotten radish!
510:
You should be ashamed! You're forty years old.
Half your lives are over.
511:
What's behind you? What do you have now?
What lies ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late. That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent. We've got to get out.
The woman doctor will tell the cops.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I took my razor to her throat.
515:
She's in the well.
You can take a look.
516:
How much time did I have?
One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten
and the apartment? Say ten!
520:
And for a measly fourteen years,
I'm going to put up with this viper?
521:
The one who put the old woman in the well?
Do what you want. I'm going to the police.
522: Go on. He won't touch you.
523:
And you two? You'll put up with him
until he kills you?
524:
Vasya, the other day I told him
I had a cold, and he...
525: Enough about your cold! Come here.
527:
- What are you up to?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Now then, comrades. The show's over.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
Once I've served my time, that's it.
I'm going straight! I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what? Watchman at my old collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could clear snow, lay bricks...
or be an interpreter. I know English.
533:
If we'd brought the hat back too!
What's the Docent? A crook.
534:
- Crooks are everywhere, but there's only one hat.
- They'd reduce our sentences for the helmet.
535:
Where did he put it?
We went everywhere, didn't we?
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was, "I'll rip your mouth off!"
537:
- Made me dive in freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
He said, "I'm fishing. You dive in."
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- "I'm fishing through a hole in the ice.
540:
Can you swim, Squint?"
- He hid the helmet in that hole!
541:
That's it! I remember now, the bad man!
It's in the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you lout?
Could've left a note before you hanged yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- They can fetch him. I'm not carrying that great lump. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing down there.
- It is there, at the bottom. You have to dive.
546:
Why me? Everything's always Squint.
Vasya, tell him to do it himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- Just now you wanted to hang yourself,
and now you're afraid of a cold!
- Sporting greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd do you in if I had the time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And there's another one back at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich! Well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
